# obol.deposits

:::caution[v3 release candidate, unreleased]

This is the reference for `@obolnetwork/obol-sdk@3.0.0-rc.12`, generated from its source and spec. Names and shapes may still change before 3.0.0, and it is not on npm `latest`. For the released SDK see the [2.x reference](../../sdk/index.md).

:::

Turns a verified lock into deposits and sends them safely: `fromLock` verifies the lock and returns the deposit data for one amount, `status` reads what the beacon chain already has for each pubkey (Obol API with EIP-6110 pending deposits, or a beacon node), and `prepareDeposit` checks credentials, signatures, OVM provenance and roles, and that a new validator does not exist yet, before building the batch or OVM deposit transactions.

## Deposit data and status {#group-reads}

### deposits.fromLock {#fromLock}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag" title="Where it reads from (spec tag)">pure</span> <span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--throws">throws 3</span> <a class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--stage" href="../lifecycle#deposit">5. Deposit</a></div>

Reads the deposit data of a cluster lock, as wei amounts ready for
[`deposits.prepareDeposit`](./deposits.md#prepareDeposit).

Checks: the lock's `fork_version` is `chainId`'s (when given);
[`cluster.verifyLock`](./cluster.md#verifyLock) passes (by default at level `attested` with the BLS
signatures (deposits and builder registration) of the returned
validators: for a 10k-validator lock about 2 s plus about 25 ms per
signature with the default backend; `verify: 'full'` for every check); every returned validator has `partial_deposit_data`
(v1.8.0+) or `deposit_data` (v1.6.0, v1.7.0), read only from the field
that version's lock hash covers (a legacy lock with `partial_deposit_data`
entries is LOCK_INVALID `partial_deposit_data_unexpected`, also with
`verify: false`); each deposit has well-formed pubkey,
credentials and signature, a positive gwei amount, the validator's group
pubkey, and a `deposit_data_root` that matches (computed when absent). A
second deposit of one amount for a validator is ignored. With `amount`,
every returned validator must have a deposit of it. Without `amount`, the
lock must hold deposit data for exactly one amount: a lock with several
(Charon's default is 1 ETH and 32 ETH) throws DEPOSIT_AMOUNT_REQUIRED
with the amounts in `details.available`; `deposits` is never left out and
an amount is never chosen for the caller.

```ts sdk-signature
obol.deposits.fromLock(
  lock: Parameters<typeof fromLock>[0],
  options?: FromLockOptions,
): Promise<LockDeposits>
```

Required when the lock holds deposit data for more than one amount (Charon's default is 1 ETH and 32 ETH per validator): the SDK never picks one, since each choice sends a different amount of ETH. Without it such a lock throws DEPOSIT_AMOUNT_REQUIRED, whose `details.available` lists the amounts. |
| <code>options.verify?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">boolean &#124; 'attested' &#124; 'full'</span> | How to run [`cluster.verifyLock`](./cluster.md#verifyLock) first: `true` / `'attested'` (default) checks the lock at level `attested` plus the BLS signatures of the returned validators; `'full'` runs every check; `false` none. |

**Example**

```ts
import { deposits } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';
import { parseEther } from 'viem';

// Verifies the lock (level 'attested' plus the deposits it returns), then
// returns the deposit data for one amount. Charon's default locks hold
// 1 ETH and 32 ETH per validator: without `amount`, DEPOSIT_AMOUNT_REQUIRED.
const { deposits: data, lockHash: hash } = await obol.deposits.fromLock(lock, { amount: parseEther('32') });
```

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: deposits.fromLock</summary>

Tag: `pure`. Inputs: `lock`, `{ amount: bigint?, verify: bool | "attested" | "full" (true), validators: (uint |
Pubkey)[]?, yieldMs: uint?, bls: BlsBackend?, publicClient: PublicClient?, publicClients? }` (the last two passed to
`verifyLock`; the bound module passes the client's `publicClient`). Output:

```
{ lockHash: Hash32, validators: uint[] (lock indexes, ascending), amounts: bigint[] (ascending),
  depositsByAmount: map bigint -> Deposit[], deposits: Deposit[] }
```

`deposits` is always present and holds one deposit per returned validator, all of one amount. An options key
outside the list above is [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID) (`unknown_key`).

`validators` picks the validators to return, by index in the lock or group pubkey (default all; one that is not in
the lock: [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID), issue `not_in_lock`). Results stay in lock order.

Checks:

1. With `verify` (`true` = `"attested"`): [`cluster.verifyLock`](./cluster.md#verifyLock) at level `attested` with `signatures` = the returned
   validators, or at level `full` for `"full"`, must pass, else [`LOCK_INVALID`](../errors.md#LOCK_INVALID) (with `step`, `issue` and `index`
   for a per-validator step). A 10k-validator lock costs about 2 s plus about 25 ms per signature checked (the
   deposits and the builder registration of each returned validator).
   (2.15 `getDepositData` ran the full verification)
2. The lock has at least one validator; each returned one has `partial_deposit_data` (v1.8.0+; `deposit_data` is
   not read) or `deposit_data` (v1.6.0, v1.7.0). Else [`LOCK_INVALID`](../errors.md#LOCK_INVALID) (issue `deposit_data_missing`). (2.15)
   Only the field the lock hash of that version covers is read, also with `verify: false`. A v1.6.0 / v1.7.0 lock
   whose validator has a non-empty `partial_deposit_data` is [`LOCK_INVALID`](../errors.md#LOCK_INVALID) (issue
   `partial_deposit_data_unexpected`, `index`): that field is outside a legacy lock's hash, so an entry there was
   not produced by the DKG (3.0.0-rc.12; before, the entry was returned in place of the signed `deposit_data`).
   Charon drops the field when reading such a lock; the SDK refuses the lock.
3. Each deposit: pubkey, credentials, signature are well-formed hex of the right length, `amount` is a positive
   integer (gwei); the pubkey equals the validator's `distributed_public_key`; a present `deposit_data_root` equals the
   recomputed root (an absent one is computed). Else [`LOCK_INVALID`](../errors.md#LOCK_INVALID) (issue `deposit_data_invalid`). (2.15)
4. Duplicate amounts for one validator keep the first. (2.15)
5. With `amount`, every returned validator has a deposit of that amount, else [`DEPOSIT_AMOUNT_NOT_IN_LOCK`](../errors.md#DEPOSIT_AMOUNT_NOT_IN_LOCK) (lists the
   available amounts). Without `amount`, the lock must hold deposit data for exactly one amount, which is returned;
   a lock with several (Charon's default is 1 ETH and 32 ETH per validator; 1, 8, 32 and 256 ETH with compounding)
   is [`DEPOSIT_AMOUNT_REQUIRED`](../errors.md#DEPOSIT_AMOUNT_REQUIRED) with `available` (the amounts every returned validator has). The SDK never picks an
   amount: each choice deposits a different amount of ETH. (3.0.0-rc.12; before, `deposits` was left out, 2.15)

The lock's `fork_version` must match the client chain when called through the client ([`LOCK_INVALID`](../errors.md#LOCK_INVALID), issue
`fork_version_mismatch`). (2.15 `getDepositData`)

### deposits.status {#status}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag" title="Where it reads from (spec tag)">api+chain</span> <span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--throws">throws 1</span> <a class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--stage" href="../lifecycle#deposit">5. Deposit</a></div>

What the beacon chain has for each pubkey: `new`, `queued` (EIP-6110 pending deposits or
a pending registry entry), `active` or `exited`, with credentials, balances and epochs
when known. From the Obol API, else a beacon node (`beaconUrl`), which is first checked
to be on the client chain and in sync. A failed or untrusted source: STATUS_UNAVAILABLE.

```ts sdk-signature
obol.deposits.status(
  pubkeys: readonly string[],
  options?: DepositStatusOptions,
): Promise<DepositStatus[]>
```

Default `{ tries: 3, delayMs: 8000 }`: up to 3 requests, waiting 8 s then 16 s (about two slots). <span class="sdk-from">from <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/core#StatusSource">StatusSource</a></span></span> |

**Example**

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: deposits.status</summary>

Tag: `api+chain`. Inputs: `pubkeys: Pubkey[]`, `{ beaconUrl: string?, lockHash: Hash32?, expectedWithdrawalAddress:
Address?, pendingRetry: { tries: 1–10?, delayMs: 0–60000? }? }`. Output per pubkey:

```
{ pubkey, status: "new" | "queued" | "active" | "exited", source: Source,
  beaconStatus: string?,      # the raw beacon name: "pending_deposit" (EIP-6110 queue only), "pending_initialized", "active_ongoing", ...
  validatorIndex: uint?, withdrawalCredentials: Hex32?, balance: bigint?, effectiveBalance: bigint?,
  activationEpoch: bigint | null?,  # registry entries: null while none is assigned (FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH)
  exitEpoch: bigint | null?,        # registry entries: null while no exit is initiated
  pendingPartialWithdrawals: bigint?,  # registry entries: sum of its EIP-7002 queue entries, wei
  pendingDeposits: { amount: bigint, withdrawalCredentials: Hex32,
                     signatureValid: bool | null? }[],  # API only; null: not checked (top-up, or pending)
  signaturesPending: bool?,         # API only; true while queued deposit signatures are being checked
  credentialsConflict: bool | null?,  # API only; null while signaturesPending
  credentialsMatch: bool | null }   # only with expectedWithdrawalAddress
```

The three epoch / queue fields are absent when the source does not report them (the interim `/v1/state/:lockHash`, an
API deployment from before they were added) and for pubkeys outside the registry; the writes then report the checks
that need them as [`VALIDATOR_STATUS_UNCHECKED`](../warnings.md#VALIDATOR_STATUS_UNCHECKED).

Mapping (beacon names): no registry entry and no pending deposit → `new`; a pending deposit (EIP-6110
`pending_deposits`) and no registry entry, or a registry entry in `pending_initialized` / `pending_queued` → `queued`;
`active_*` → `active`; `exited_*` / `withdrawal_*` → `exited`.

**Which credentials apply** (the _effective credentials_). A registered validator has its own. For a pubkey only in the
queue, the beacon chain skips queued deposits with an invalid BLS signature until the first valid one creates the
validator, so the effective credentials are those of the first queued deposit that is not `signatureValid: false` and
is either `signatureValid: true` or has non-zero credentials (an unchecked zero-credential top-up has no valid
signature for a new validator). With the Obol API's signature checks they are the first validly signed deposit's once
every deposit before it is checked, even while later ones are still pending (those are top-ups); while an unchecked
deposit (`signatureValid: null`) comes before the first valid one there are none (undecided, never guessed).

`credentialsMatch`: the effective credentials are `0x01` / `0x02` + 11 zero bytes + `expectedWithdrawalAddress`
(case-insensitive); `null` when there are none yet (`new`, every queued deposit invalid, or undecided while
`signaturesPending`).

Queued deposit signatures (Obol API only). The API checks the signature of each queued deposit of a pubkey not in the
registry (deposit domain, genesis fork version), in the background, usually within a slot:

- `signaturesPending: true` while they are not all checked; `false` for registered and new pubkeys. While pending,
  `credentialsConflict` is `null` and each unchecked deposit has `signatureValid: null`.
- `signatureValid`: `true` / `false` for a queue-only pubkey's deposit, `null` when not checked (a registered
  validator's queued top-up, whose signature does not matter, or still pending).
- `credentialsConflict: true` when validly signed queued deposits carry different non-zero credentials; the first one
  applies.
- A queue-only entry's `withdrawalCredentials`: the API walks the queue in order and stops at the first deposit that
  is `signatureValid: null` (credentials `null`, undecided) or `true` (that deposit's credentials, which the chain
  will apply: later deposits are top-ups). So they are the first validly signed deposit's when every deposit before
  it is checked, possibly while `signaturesPending: true`, and absent otherwise (none valid, or an unchecked deposit
  first).

When an entry of a batch has `signaturesPending: true`, `deposits.status` re-reads that batch, up to
`pendingRetry.tries` requests in all (default 3), waiting `pendingRetry.delayMs` (default 8000) before the first
retry and twice as long before each later one (8 s, then 16 s: about two slots). An entry still pending after that is
returned with `signaturesPending: true`; `deposits.status` does not throw for it, the writes do (`prepareDeposit`
check 5). An API answer without these fields (a deployment from before them) leaves them absent, and the deposits are
treated as possibly valid, as with the beacon fallback.

Sources, in order:

1. API: `POST /v1/validators/:network/deposit-status` with `{ pubkeys }`, at most 500 distinct pubkeys per request
   (the API's limit; larger inputs are batched). Answer `{ validators: [{ pubkey, status, beaconStatus, index,
balance, effectiveBalance, activationEpoch, exitEpoch, pendingPartialWithdrawals, withdrawalCredentials,
signaturesPending, credentialsConflict, pendingDeposits: [{ amount, withdrawalCredentials, signatureValid }] }] }`,
   one entry per requested pubkey, amounts and balances as wei decimal
   strings, epochs as decimal strings (`null` for FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH or no registry entry), `pendingPartialWithdrawals`
   the wei sum (`"0"` when none), `null` where there is nothing (obol-api #1047). A malformed epoch or sum is
   [`STATUS_UNAVAILABLE`](../errors.md#STATUS_UNAVAILABLE). Every requested
   pubkey must be answered exactly once, `status` must be the mapping of `beaconStatus`, a registry entry needs an
   index, credentials and balances, a queue-only entry at least one queued deposit, a `new` one none. The signature
   fields must agree: `signaturesPending: true` only on a queue-only entry and only with `credentialsConflict: null`
   (`null` otherwise is malformed); a queue-only entry with checked deposits has `withdrawalCredentials` equal to the
   first validly signed deposit's when every deposit before it is checked, and `null` otherwise (none valid, or a
   `signatureValid: null` before the first valid one), pending or not; once not pending it has no `signatureValid:
null`, and `credentialsConflict` matches its validly signed deposits. A signature check that fails on the API side
   is an HTTP 502 for the pending entries (not cached), handled as any other API failure below.
2. While that route answers 404 (not deployed yet): with `lockHash`, the interim `GET /v1/state/:lockHash` (with
   `pending_deposit`), which answers by lock: the lock is fetched first, a pubkey not in it is [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID) (issue
   `not_in_lock`), a pubkey the lock has but `/state` leaves out is `new`, and a registry validator's queued top-ups
   come as one amount without credentials. Without `lockHash` and without `beaconUrl`: [`STATUS_UNAVAILABLE`](../errors.md#STATUS_UNAVAILABLE) (details
   `reason: "endpoint_unavailable"`, hint: pass `lockHash` or `beaconUrl`).
3. Chain fallback with `beaconUrl`, when the API is off, is unavailable, or lacks the route without `lockHash`.
   "Unavailable" is [`API_TIMEOUT`](../errors.md#API_TIMEOUT), or [`API_ERROR`](../errors.md#API_ERROR) with no HTTP status (a network failure) or a 5xx. Any other API
   answer is thrown and the beacon node is not asked: 400 / 422 ([`API_VALIDATION`](../errors.md#API_VALIDATION)), 401 / 403
   ([`API_UNAUTHORIZED`](../errors.md#API_UNAUTHORIZED)), 409, 429 ([`API_RATE_LIMIT`](../errors.md#API_RATE_LIMIT)), 451, [`API_RESPONSE_MISMATCH`](../errors.md#API_RESPONSE_MISMATCH), and a 404 from the by-lock
   routes of 2. (the API does not know that lock). A 404 from the deposit-status route itself is the route being
   absent (it answers `new` for an unknown pubkey, never 404), which is 2. (3.0.0-rc.12; before, every API error
   fell back.)

   Before any state is read the node is checked (3.0.0-rc.12), and a failed check is [`STATUS_UNAVAILABLE`](../errors.md#STATUS_UNAVAILABLE), never
   "every pubkey is `new`":
   - `GET /eth/v1/beacon/genesis`: `genesis_validators_root` equals the client chain's (chain table), else
     `reason: "beacon_wrong_chain"`;
   - `GET /eth/v1/node/syncing`: `is_syncing` is `false` and `el_offline` is not `true`, else `reason:
"beacon_syncing"`; `is_optimistic` is not `true`, else `reason: "beacon_optimistic"` (`el_offline` and
     `is_optimistic` may be absent on older nodes);
   - every state answer below with `execution_optimistic: true` is refused (`reason: "beacon_optimistic"`).

   Then: `GET /eth/v1/beacon/states/head/pending_deposits`, then `GET
/eth/v1/beacon/states/head/pending_partial_withdrawals` (summed per validator index) and `POST
/eth/v1/beacon/states/head/validators` (with `validator.activation_epoch`, `exit_epoch`, `effective_balance`); the
   pending queue is read before the registry so a deposit moving from the queue to the registry is not missed (2.16
   `existingDeposits.ts`). A beacon node does not check queued deposit signatures: the signature fields are absent,
   every queued deposit counts as possibly valid, and a queue-only pubkey's `withdrawalCredentials` are its first
   queued deposit's. So a queued deposit with an invalid signature and other credentials is reported there as a
   [`DEPOSIT_CONFLICT`](../errors.md#DEPOSIT_CONFLICT) by `prepareDeposit` (fails closed), where the API would skip it. The interim `/v1/state` source
   (2.) has no signature fields either.

Without API and `beaconUrl`: [`API_DISABLED`](../errors.md#API_DISABLED). A malformed or incomplete answer (missing pubkey, duplicate result, bad
credentials, unknown status) or a failed beacon request is [`STATUS_UNAVAILABLE`](../errors.md#STATUS_UNAVAILABLE), never a guessed `new`. (2.16)

The writes that read status (`prepareDeposit`, `prepareWithdraw`, `prepareConsolidate`, `prepareEoaWithdraw`) take
the same `beaconUrl` / `lockHash` / `pendingRetry` options ([`StatusSource`](./types/core.md#StatusSource)). A source that is configured and fails makes the write throw; the status
checks are skipped (with [`DEPOSIT_EXISTENCE_UNCHECKED`](../warnings.md#DEPOSIT_EXISTENCE_UNCHECKED) for deposits) only when there is no source at all, which
includes an API without the deposit-status route and neither `lockHash` nor `beaconUrl` (`reason:
"endpoint_unavailable"` above).

`queued` is deliberately broad; `beaconStatus` tells the cases apart. They behave differently for a second deposit:
a registry `pending_initialized` / `pending_queued` validator can still take the rest of a chunked activation deposit,
while an app may refuse further deposits to a `pending_deposit` pubkey until the queue processes it (the launchpad
does). `beaconStatus` is `"pending_deposit"` for a pubkey only in the queue and absent for `new`.

</details>

## Checks {#group-checks}

### deposits.assertDepositData {#assertDepositData}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag" title="Where it reads from (spec tag)">pure</span> <span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--throws">throws 3</span> <span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--since" title="Renamed in 3.0.0-rc.12">rc.12: was deposits.verifyDepositData</span> <a class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--stage" href="../lifecycle#deposit">5. Deposit</a></div>

Checks deposits before ETH is sent, in order for each deposit, then the
signatures:

1. `kind: 'deposit'` with an all-zero signature: DEPOSIT_LOOKS_LIKE_TOP_UP;
2. `amount` is whole gwei and at least 1 ETH;
3. credentials prefix is `0x00`, `0x01` or `0x02`, and `0x01` / `0x02`
   have 11 zero bytes after it;
4. `amount` is at most 2048 ETH for `0x02` credentials or a top-up, else
   32 ETH;
5. with `expectedWithdrawalAddress`, the credentials are `0x01` / `0x02`
   for it (case-insensitive); a top-up may instead have all-zero
   credentials;
6. `depositDataRoot` is the SSZ root of the deposit;
7. for `kind: 'deposit'`, every BLS signature is valid in the deposit
   domain of the chain's genesis fork (randomised batches of 32, each
   signature must be valid on its own; the first invalid index is
   reported). The work yields to the event loop every `yieldMs`.

With `options.signal`, an abort stops the signature checks at the next
yield point.

```ts sdk-signature
obol.deposits.assertDepositData(
  deposits: readonly DepositInput[],
  options?: Partial<AssertDepositDataOptions>,
): Promise<void>
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>deposits</code> | <span class="sdk-type">readonly <a href="./types/core#DepositInput">DepositInput</a>[]</span> |  |
| <code>options?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">Partial&lt;<a href="./types/deposits#AssertDepositDataOptions">AssertDepositDataOptions</a>&gt;</span> |  |

</div>

**Returns** <span class="sdk-type">Promise&lt;void&gt;</span>

**Throws** <span class="sdk-muted">(per spec)</span> <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--error" href="../errors#ABORTED">ABORTED</a> <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--error" href="../errors#DEPOSIT_INVALID">DEPOSIT_INVALID</a> <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--error" href="../errors#DEPOSIT_LOOKS_LIKE_TOP_UP">DEPOSIT_LOOKS_LIKE_TOP_UP</a> <span class="sdk-muted">plus the [checks every operation runs](../errors.md#checks-every-operation-runs)</span>

**Example**

```ts
import { deposits } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';

// Throws DEPOSIT_INVALID with the failing `index` and `issue`; resolves otherwise.
await deposits.assertDepositData(depositData, { chainId: 560048, expectedWithdrawalAddress: ovmAddress });
```

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: deposits.assertDepositData</summary>

Named `deposits.verifyDepositData` until 3.0.0-rc.12: it throws when a check fails and returns nothing.

Tag: `pure`. Inputs: `deposits: Deposit[]`, `{ chainId: uint, kind: "deposit" | "topUp" (default "deposit"),
expectedWithdrawalAddress: Address?, yieldMs: uint?, signal: AbortSignal?, bls: BlsBackend? }`. Output: nothing
(throws on the first failure).

For each deposit in order, then the signatures (vectors `deposit_checks.json`):

1. `kind` is `deposit` and the signature is all zero: [`DEPOSIT_LOOKS_LIKE_TOP_UP`](../errors.md#DEPOSIT_LOOKS_LIKE_TOP_UP). A zero-signature deposit to a new
   validator is ignored by the beacon chain and the ETH is not recoverable. (2.15)
2. `amount` is whole gwei (`amount_not_whole_gwei`) and ≥ 1 ETH (`amount_below_minimum`). (2.15)
3. Credentials prefix is `0x00`, `0x01` or `0x02` (`credentials_prefix_unknown`); for `0x01` / `0x02`, bytes 1–11 are
   zero (`credentials_malformed`). (2.15)
4. `amount` ≤ 2048 ETH if the prefix is `0x02` or `kind` is `topUp`, else ≤ 32 ETH (`amount_above_maximum`). (2.15)
5. With `expectedWithdrawalAddress`: the prefix is not `0x00` and the last 20 bytes equal it, case-insensitive
   (`credentials_mismatch`); a `topUp` may instead have all-zero credentials. (2.15)
6. `depositDataRoot` equals `hash_tree_root(DepositData{pubkey, withdrawal_credentials, amount_gwei, signature})`
   (`root_mismatch`). (2.15)
7. `kind` is `deposit`: the chain must have a known genesis fork ([`UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN`](../errors.md#UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN)); every signature verifies
   against the pubkey over `DepositMessage{pubkey, withdrawal_credentials, amount_gwei}` in the deposit domain
   (`DOMAIN_DEPOSIT 0x03000000`, genesis fork version, zero genesis validators root). Batch-verified as in
   [`cluster.verifyLock`](./cluster.md#verifyLock) (random weights, so each signature must be valid on its own); on failure the first invalid
   index is reported (`signature_invalid`; a signature or pubkey that is not a valid point also counts). Options
   `yieldMs`, `signal` ([`ABORTED`](../errors.md#ABORTED)) and `bls` as for `verifyLock`. (2.15; `signal` new in rc.6)

Failures 2–7 are [`DEPOSIT_INVALID`](../errors.md#DEPOSIT_INVALID) with `issue` and `index`.

<p class="sdk-muted">From <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/spec/operations.md">spec/operations.md</a>.</p>

</details>

<p class="sdk-see">See also: <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/spec/operations.md#depositsassertdepositdata">spec/operations.md</a> · <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/spec/schemas/deposits.assertDepositData.json">input JSON Schema</a> · <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/src/deposits/index.ts#L44">source</a></p>

## Transactions {#group-transactions}

### deposits.prepareDeposit {#prepareDeposit}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--tag" title="Where it reads from (spec tag)">chain (uses deposits</span> <span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--throws">throws 11</span> <span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--warning">6 warnings</span> <a class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--stage" href="../lifecycle#deposit">5. Deposit</a></div>

Prepares deposits via an OVM (`via: { ovm }`) or the batch deposit contract
(`via: { batch: true }`). Checks the deposit data, OVM provenance (on chain) and the
sender's DEPOSIT role, and, with a status source, that a `kind: 'deposit'` validator
does not exist yet (DEPOSIT_VALIDATOR_EXISTS, or DEPOSIT_CONFLICT when its credentials
are someone else's). Returns one [`Prepared`](./types/send.md#Prepared) per transaction (OVM deposits one each;
one per 500 deposits via the batch contract.

```ts sdk-signature
obol.deposits.prepareDeposit(
  input: PrepareDepositInput,
): Promise<Array<Prepared<'deposit'>>>
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>input</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/deposits#PrepareDepositInput">PrepareDepositInput</a></span> |  |
| <code>input.deposits</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/core#DepositInput">DepositInput</a>[]</span> |  |
| <code>input.kind?</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/core#DepositKind">DepositKind</a></span> |  |
| <code>input.via</code> | <span class="sdk-type">{ ovm: string } &#124; { batch: true }</span> |  |
| <code>input.expectedWithdrawalAddress?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> | Required with batch; with ovm it is the OVM address. |
| <code>input.from?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> | Sender for the OVM role check; default the wallet account. |
| <code>input.beaconUrl?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> | Beacon node REST URL, for the chain fallback. <span class="sdk-from">from <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/core#StatusSource">StatusSource</a></span></span> |
| <code>input.lockHash?</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> | The cluster lock of the pubkeys: only needed while the Obol API does not serve the deposit-status route (the interim `GET /v1/state/:lockHash` answers by lock). <span class="sdk-from">from <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/core#StatusSource">StatusSource</a></span></span> |
| <code>input.pendingRetry?</code> | <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/core#PendingRetry">PendingRetry</a></span> | Re-reads of an Obol API deposit-status batch while an entry has `signaturesPending` (the API checks queued deposit signatures in the background, usually within a slot). Default `{ tries: 3, delayMs: 8000 }`: up to 3 requests, waiting 8 s then 16 s (about two slots). <span class="sdk-from">from <span class="sdk-type"><a href="./types/core#StatusSource">StatusSource</a></span></span> |

Send it with [`obol.send`](./send.md#send) or your wallet layer.

**Can report** <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--warning" href="../warnings#DEPOSIT_EXISTENCE_UNCHECKED" title="warning">DEPOSIT_EXISTENCE_UNCHECKED</a> <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--info" href="../warnings#DEPOSIT_ALREADY_QUEUED" title="info">DEPOSIT_ALREADY_QUEUED</a> <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--warning" href="../warnings#QUEUED_CREDENTIALS_CONFLICT" title="warning">QUEUED_CREDENTIALS_CONFLICT</a> <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--warning" href="../warnings#TOP_UP_ABOVE_EFFECTIVE_CAP" title="warning">TOP_UP_ABOVE_EFFECTIVE_CAP</a> <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--warning" href="../warnings#TOP_UP_EXITED_VALIDATOR" title="warning">TOP_UP_EXITED_VALIDATOR</a> <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--warning" href="../warnings#TOP_UP_CREDENTIALS_FOREIGN" title="warning">TOP_UP_CREDENTIALS_FOREIGN</a> <a class="sdk-chip sdk-chip--warning" href="../warnings#OVM_STAKE_NOT_TRACKED" title="warning">OVM_STAKE_NOT_TRACKED</a>

**Example**

```ts
import { deposits } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';

const prepared = await obol.deposits.prepareDeposit({
  deposits: depositData,
  via: { ovm: ovmAddress }, // or { batch: true } with expectedWithdrawalAddress
  // kind: 'topUp', // to add stake to validators that exist
});
for (const tx of prepared) {
  const sent = await obol.send(tx); // FINDINGS_NOT_ACKNOWLEDGED if tx.checks has a warning
  await sent.wait();
}
```

<details class="sdk-spec">
<summary>Specification: deposits.prepareDeposit</summary>

Tag: `chain` (uses [`deposits.status`](./deposits.md#status) when available). Inputs:

```
{ deposits: Deposit[], kind: "deposit" | "topUp" (default "deposit"),
  via: { ovm: Address } | { batch: true },          # OVM.deposit, or the batch deposit contract
  expectedWithdrawalAddress: Address?,               # required with batch; with ovm it is the OVM address
  from: Address? }                                   # sender, for the role check; default the wallet account
```

Checks:

1. [`deposits.assertDepositData`](./deposits.md#assertDepositData) with `expectedWithdrawalAddress` = the OVM address (via ovm) or the given address
   (via batch; required, [`PAYLOAD_INVALID`](../errors.md#PAYLOAD_INVALID)). (2.15; 2.15 let `eoa.deposit` omit the address, v3 does not)
2. Via ovm: [`ovm.getProvenance(ovm)`](./ovm.md#getProvenance) is `obol`, else [`OVM_NOT_OBOL`](../errors.md#OVM_NOT_OBOL) (notObol) or [`PROVENANCE_UNKNOWN`](../errors.md#PROVENANCE_UNKNOWN) (unknown). The
   principal is at stake, so unknown is an error here. (new; 2.16 rule)
3. Via ovm: the sender is the owner or holds `DEPOSIT_ROLE` (`owner()`, `rolesOf(from)`), else [`OVM_ROLE_MISSING`](../errors.md#OVM_ROLE_MISSING)
   (the call would revert). (new)
4. Via batch with credentials pointing at a contract that [`ovm.getProvenance`](./ovm.md#getProvenance) says is `obol`: Finding [`OVM_STAKE_NOT_TRACKED`](../warnings.md#OVM_STAKE_NOT_TRACKED)
   (warning). The batch contract does not raise `amountOfPrincipalStake`, so the principal would later be routed as
   rewards unless the owner calls `setAmountOfPrincipalStake`. (new; from `ObolValidatorManager.deposit`)
5. Existence, when [`deposits.status`](./deposits.md#status) can answer (API or `beaconUrl`; else Finding [`DEPOSIT_EXISTENCE_UNCHECKED`](../warnings.md#DEPOSIT_EXISTENCE_UNCHECKED),
   a warning since 3.0.0-rc.12: `send` needs it acknowledged). "The expected address" is the OVM (via ovm) or
   `expectedWithdrawalAddress` (via batch):
   - queue only, `signaturesPending` still true after the `pendingRetry` re-reads, and the credentials undecided (an
     unchecked deposit before the first valid one) → [`STATUS_UNAVAILABLE`](../errors.md#STATUS_UNAVAILABLE) (details `reason: "signatures_pending"`,
     `pubkey`; hint: retry in a slot or two): which deposit creates the validator, and so its credentials, is not
     known yet, and is never guessed (any `kind`) (new). Once decided, the write proceeds with them; the unchecked
     later deposits count as possibly valid in the conflict check below (conservative);
   - queued deposits with `signatureValid: false` are left out of the rest of this check (they never reach the
     validator); `null` or absent counts as possibly valid;
   - `credentialsConflict: true` (validly signed queued deposits disagree; the first one applies): [`DEPOSIT_CONFLICT`](../errors.md#DEPOSIT_CONFLICT)
     (`existingCredentials` = the first validly signed deposit's) when this deposit's credentials differ from it,
     else Finding [`QUEUED_CREDENTIALS_CONFLICT`](../warnings.md#QUEUED_CREDENTIALS_CONFLICT) (warning, subject the pubkey) (new);
   - otherwise, a possibly valid pending deposit for the pubkey has different or unknown credentials →
     [`DEPOSIT_CONFLICT`](../errors.md#DEPOSIT_CONFLICT) (2.16); a queued deposit with all-zero credentials (a top-up, which cannot create the
     validator) is not a conflict unless it is `signatureValid: true`;
   - a top-up with all-zero credentials checks no credentials (it does not fix them), so it gets neither
     [`DEPOSIT_CONFLICT`](../errors.md#DEPOSIT_CONFLICT) nor, on `credentialsConflict`, more than the warning;
   - `kind: "topUp"` and the pubkey is `new`, or only in the queue with every queued deposit `signatureValid: false`
     → [`DEPOSIT_TOP_UP_TARGET_MISSING`](../errors.md#DEPOSIT_TOP_UP_TARGET_MISSING) (new);
   - `kind: "deposit"` and the pubkey is already in the validator registry, in any status (`pending_initialized`
     through `withdrawal_done`): always an error (3.0.0-rc.12; before, the warning `DEPOSIT_IS_TOP_UP`). The beacon
     chain applies such a deposit as a top-up and ignores its withdrawal credentials, so the ETH follows the ones
     the validator has:
     - they are not `0x01` / `0x02` credentials of the expected address, or are unknown → [`DEPOSIT_CONFLICT`](../errors.md#DEPOSIT_CONFLICT)
       (`existing: "validator"`, `existingCredentials`). The deposit front-running case: the validator was created
       first with someone else's withdrawal address;
     - they are → [`DEPOSIT_VALIDATOR_EXISTS`](../errors.md#DEPOSIT_VALIDATOR_EXISTS) (`status`, `withdrawalCredentials`). Adding stake to an existing
       validator is `kind: "topUp"`;
   - `kind: "topUp"` and the credentials the validator has (registry), or will get (the first possibly valid queued
     deposit), do not point at the expected address → Finding [`TOP_UP_CREDENTIALS_FOREIGN`](../warnings.md#TOP_UP_CREDENTIALS_FOREIGN) (warning: the top-up can
     only be withdrawn to those credentials; a top-up to a validator the caller does not control is a donation, so
     `send` refuses it until acknowledged) (3.0.0-rc.12);
   - same-credential deposits already queued (possibly valid ones) → Finding [`DEPOSIT_ALREADY_QUEUED`](../warnings.md#DEPOSIT_ALREADY_QUEUED) (info) (2.16);
   - `kind: "topUp"` to an `exited` validator → Finding [`TOP_UP_EXITED_VALIDATOR`](../warnings.md#TOP_UP_EXITED_VALIDATOR) (warning) (new);
   - the validator has `0x01` (or `0x00`) credentials and `balance` + queued amounts + this deposit > 32 ETH →
     Finding [`TOP_UP_ABOVE_EFFECTIVE_CAP`](../warnings.md#TOP_UP_ABOVE_EFFECTIVE_CAP) (warning; queued amounts without `signatureValid: false`: the excess is swept back to the withdrawal address by the next
     partial-withdrawal sweep, not staked) (new).

   [`DEPOSIT_ALREADY_QUEUED`](../warnings.md#DEPOSIT_ALREADY_QUEUED) is info because a chunked activation deposit is legitimate. An app may treat it as a stop
   for `beaconStatus = "pending_deposit"`.

6. The target contract has code: the OVM (2.15 implicit), or the chain's batch deposit contract
   (`0xcD7a6C118Ac8F6544BC5076F2D8Fb86D2C546756` mainnet, `0x4c9506eE2fCd962f03022D9d8ebf6f7828abEfaf` Hoodi), else
   [`CONTRACT_NOT_AVAILABLE`](../errors.md#CONTRACT_NOT_AVAILABLE).

Output: `Prepared<"deposit">[]` (preview [`DepositPreview`](./types/deposits.md#DepositPreview)):

- via ovm: one per deposit (through Multicall3 the OVM would see Multicall3 as the sender, and anyone can call
  Multicall3, so it must not hold `DEPOSIT_ROLE`), `OVM.deposit(pubkey, withdrawal_credentials,
signature, deposit_data_root)`, `value = amount`. (2.15 `depositOVM`)
- via batch: one per 500 deposits, `batchDeposit((pubKey, withdrawalCredentials, signature, amount)[])` (the
  contract computes each deposit data root itself; check 1 has already verified ours), `value` = sum of amounts.
  (2.15 `submitEOABatchDeposit`)

`DepositPreview = { pubkeys: Pubkey[], total: bigint, kind }`.

A Safe that holds `DEPOSIT_ROLE` can still deposit to several validators with one signature: it batches the
`Prepared[]` requests with Safe `MultiSend` (a `delegatecall`, so the Safe stays `msg.sender` and its role applies).
Planning top-ups (how much each validator needs to reach the next whole-ETH effective balance) is left to the app.

<p class="sdk-muted">From <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/spec/operations.md">spec/operations.md</a>.</p>

</details>

<p class="sdk-see">See also: <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/spec/operations.md#depositspreparedeposit">spec/operations.md</a> · <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/spec/schemas/deposits.prepareDeposit.json">input JSON Schema</a> · <a href="https://github.com/ObolNetwork/obol-sdk/blob/080fa554c999b11c014f3f09be26274014ded0b9/src/deposits/index.ts#L72">source</a></p>

### deposits.depositDataRoot {#depositDataRoot}

<div class="sdk-badges"><span class="sdk-badge sdk-badge--pure" title="Exported from the namespace, not bound on the client">namespace only</span></div>

SSZ hash_tree_root of DepositData; `amountGwei` as on the wire.

```ts sdk-signature
deposits.depositDataRoot(fields: {
  pubkey: string;
  withdrawalCredentials: string;
  amountGwei: bigint;
  signature: string;
}): Hex
```

<div class="sdk-table sdk-table--fields">

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <code>fields</code> | <span class="sdk-type">{ pubkey: string; withdrawalCredentials: string; amountGwei: bigint; signature: string; }</span> |  |
| <code>fields.pubkey</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> |  |
| <code>fields.withdrawalCredentials</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> |  |
| <code>fields.amountGwei</code> | <span class="sdk-type">bigint</span> |  |
| <code>fields.signature</code> | <span class="sdk-type">string</span> |  |

</div>

**Returns** <span class="sdk-type">Hex</span>

**Example**

```ts
import { deposits } from '@obolnetwork/obol-sdk';

const d = depositData[0];
const root = deposits.depositDataRoot({
  pubkey: d.pubkey,
  withdrawalCredentials: d.withdrawalCredentials,
  amountGwei: d.amount / 1_000_000_000n,
  signature: d.signature,
});
if (root !== d.depositDataRoot) throw new Error('deposit data root mismatch');
```
